prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Dissolved material in runoff: A narrow clear teal runoff ribbon leaves the roughened basalt face, no visible particles suspended in it. Avoid: Dissolved ions are invisible; label carries chemistry, never add sparkling salt grains.
2. A sea receiving dissolved minerals: The established broad early sea receives a clear narrow stream along its rocky edge, ordinary unchanged teal water. Avoid: Same sea, no invented mineral colour or bag of salt; route supplies context.
3. Fine particles loosened from rock: A small fan of fine charcoal grains and crumbs loosens from a rough wet basalt edge. Avoid: Visible solid fragments, not invisible ions or biologically formed soil.
4. Sediment suspended in runoff: A shallow teal runoff ribbon carries a clearly visible soft charcoal sediment cloud trailing from a rock edge. Avoid: Cloudiness is suspended solid material; no clear-water false chemical colouring.
5. A bed of fine sediment: A sheltered underwater cutaway shows a thin flat dark sediment layer building on rock below clear teal water. Avoid: Settled fine bed rather than drifting cloud or emerged sandy beach.
6. Hot rock beneath the seafloor: A dark seafloor cutaway encloses a broad amber hot-rock region well below a thin teal water layer. Avoid: Heat remains buried beneath existing sea; no exposed lava shoreline.
7. Open fractures in the seafloor: A broad dark seafloor slab beneath teal water has two connected deep fissures and an unbroken central block. Avoid: Submerged rock context; no circulation or mineral vent already operating.
8. Cooler surrounding seawater: A deep clear teal water column above a small dark seafloor edge, subtle horizontal cool tonal layers. Avoid: Ordinary surrounding water; temperature distinction contextual, no ice crystals.
9. Seawater entering the crust: Teal sea water enters the left fissure of the established seafloor cutaway, one short downward cue. Avoid: Seawater source visibly above; do not turn it into a land spring.
10. Water heated inside the crust: The same subsurface teal route passes beside the amber buried hot-rock zone, no exposed surface discharge. Avoid: Heating shown through contact, not liquid water magically becoming orange magma.
11. Hydrothermal fluid carrying dissolved material: The same confined water route runs along rough reactive rock faces near buried heat, remaining visually clear. Avoid: Dissolved constituents invisible; no floating crystals before precipitation.
12. Hot fluid returning through fractures: A clear subsurface water route curves from the hot zone up the right seafloor fissure toward its mouth. Avoid: Upward route shown by one sparse cue; no plume or chimney yet.
13. Minerals precipitating at a vent: At a low seafloor fissure mouth, tiny pale and charcoal particles appear where fluid meets teal seawater. Avoid: New visible solids at mixing boundary, no smoke or tall finished vent tower.
14. A hydrothermal plume: A soft tapering charcoal-and-ivory particle plume rises from a low seafloor crack into surrounding teal water. Avoid: Submerged mineral suspension, not atmospheric smoke or a flaming volcano.
15. Mineral deposits around a seafloor outlet: A modest irregular mineral crust and low mound surround a small underwater fissure outlet. Avoid: Low accumulated deposit, no towering black-smoker chimney, worms or organisms.
16. Wind across the water: Three long sparse curved air strokes pass over a teal sea edge with only small incipient ripples. Avoid: Air motion above water, not a giant wave, tide or mechanical fan.

Image2 is the APPROVED COAST GEOGRAPHY reference. For any shore or pool subject keep its stepped LEFT headland and low RIGHT ridge. Any hollows/pools are the same threebasins: LARGE foreground-right pool, smaller mid-left pool and small distant middle pool, same connecting basalt rims. Waterlevel orlighting maychange; rockgeometry andcamera mustnot. Water-chemistry detailviews may use closer crops of these materials. No invented bottles, vessels, observers or biological scenery.
